sub_answers.text: States allocate electoral votes equal to their number of congressional districts plus two senators [d20539685s6p0]. Voters cast ballots for slates of electors who pledge to vote for their candidate and running mate [d20539685s6p0]. Electors meet in their respective state capitols to cast their Electoral College votes on a designated meeting day in December [d20539685s6p0].

sub_answers.text: All candidates who appear on the ballot or qualify for write-in votes must submit a list of electors pledged to their ticket [d20539685s6p0]. Voters technically cast ballots for electors rather than directly for presidential candidates [d20539685s6p0]. Election law governs voter registration, ballot access, and procedures for absentee ballots and related election administration functions [d864164s0p0].

sub_answers.text: Electors from each state meet separately in their state capitols to formally cast Electoral College votes rather than meeting as a single national body [d20539685s6p0]. Election law covers the regulation of election management bodies, voting, counting of votes, and scrutiny procedures [d864164s0p0].

sub_answers.text: Ballot curing is a process that allows voters to correct minor errors on mail-in or absentee ballots to address voter identification issues [d78408403s0p0]. Ballot curing can reduce rejected mail ballots and improve voter trust and participation [d78408403s0p0]. Ballot curing rules vary by state and are not universally available [d78408403s0p0].

Describe the legal method Maryland used to allocate presidential electors for 2008 (e.g., statewide winner-take-all, by congressional district, or other), cite the applicable state statutes or constitutional provisions, and state the exact number of electoral votes Maryland had for the 2008 election (including how that number was determined).
sub_answers.text:
Forty-eight states use a statewide winner-take-all system to award their electors to the statewide popular vote winner [d77541080s2p0].
Electoral votes for each state equal the sum of its U.S. senators and representatives as allocated for that census apportionment [d77541080s2p0].
Electoral votes are certified by state electors in December after the election [d77541080s2p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Detail the 2008 Maryland procedures governing ballot access and candidate qualification (filing deadlines, petition signature thresholds, minor-party and independent candidate rules), voter registration rules and deadlines (including eligibility checks, same-day or deadline dates, and any online or mail options), and absentee voting policy in effect in 2008 (application deadlines, reasons required or no-excuse, ballot return methods, and processing rules).
sub_answers.text:
Two-thirds of U.S. states require election officials to notify voters of a missing signature or a signature discrepancy and allow an opportunity to cure the ballot [d78408403s3p0].
Notification methods and time frames for curing vary by state and may include mail, email, phone, text, or sending a replacement ballot [d78408403s3p0].
Non-governmental organizations sometimes contact voters identified in a state's database of challenged ballots during the curing process [d78408403s3p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe how Maryland ran polling places and counted votes for the 2008 presidential election: official poll opening/closing hours, voter check-in and provisional-ballot procedures, poll-worker training and chain-of-custody protocols, the types and vendors of voting equipment used at precincts (paper ballot, optical scanner, DRE, etc.), how ballots were tabulated (precinct scanners vs. central counting), and procedures for tally reporting and certification.
sub_answers.text:
For early U.S. presidential elections, voters sometimes voted directly for individual electors rather than for a presidential ticket, which could yield small differences among electors pledged to the same candidate [d40507s10p0].
The Electoral College itself never meets as one body; electors from each state meet in their respective state capitols to cast their electoral votes [d20539685s6p0].
Electoral votes are cast by state electors in December and later certified by Congress on January 6 [d77541080s2p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Identify any electoral-administration changes in Maryland implemented before the 2008 presidential election, including legislative or court-ordered redistricting actions after the 2000 census, precinct boundary or polling-place consolidations, changes to county election board structures or officials, and the adoption or certification of new voting systems or administrative rules affecting the 2008 election.
sub_answers.text:
Maryland used single-member electoral districts to choose some electors in early 19th-century elections, as in 1832 and as discussed in 1816-era election practices [d39096094s0p0][d40507s10p0].
Maine adopted the congressional district method in 1972, awarding two statewide electors to the state winner and one elector per congressional district [d40568s12p0].
The composition of a state's electoral vote total has historically depended on its number of senators and representatives, which can change after each census apportionment [d77541080s2p0].

By what legal mechanism does Maryland assign its presidential electors (e.g., statewide winner-take-all, congressional district method), what statute or code section governs that allocation, and how many electors did Maryland appoint for the 2008 Electoral College?
sub_answers.text:
In the 1832 presidential election Maryland's electors were chosen in single-member district elections rather than by a statewide winner-take-all method [d39096094s0p0].
A total of ten electoral votes were allocated to Maryland in the 1832 election [d39096094s0p0].
Historical nineteenth-century election practice sometimes required voters to vote directly for individual electors, producing vote differences among electors pledged to the same candidate [d40507s10p0].
Electors are pledged to their candidate and running mate but are not legally obligated to vote for them and an elector who votes otherwise is known as a faithless elector [d20539685s6p0].
